transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, doctor, what brings me in is that I just keep messing up little things lately. It's nothing huge, but it's frustrating. Like, I'll write down the wrong time on the sign-up sheet for a class at the senior center, or I'll be working on a project in the garage, measure a board, and still cut it a hair short just because I skipped over the small lines on the tape measure. It's just... careless stuff like that.
Have you always been someone who makes these kinds of careless mistakes, or is this something new that's been happening recently?

Well, I suppose I might have always had my moments here and there, but... it's really been noticeably interfering since we moved into the condo. That was right about a year and a month ago. So, I guess it feels more recent that it's actually become a real bother and started getting in the way of things.
Besides these careless mistakes, have you noticed any changes in your memory or ability to concentrate over this past year?
No, not really. My memory seems fine, and I can concentrate alright when I need to. It's just those little slip-ups I mentioned.
Over this past year since you moved, have you noticed any changes in your mood? For example, do you feel sadder, more worried, or more irritable than you used to?

No, my mood's been pretty steady, really. I haven't been feeling sad or down or anything like that. I'm not any more worried than usual. Maybe a little annoyed with myself when I make those stupid mistakes, but not irritable in general. Just... regular, I guess.
Since you moved to the condo a year ago, have these careless mistakes been getting progressively worse, or have they stayed about the same level?
I'd say they've stayed about the same level. I haven't really noticed them getting progressively worse or anything like that. It's just been a pretty steady annoyance since we got settled in.
Have you noticed any changes in how you speak or communicate, or have people commented that you seem different in your personality or behavior since the move?

No, nothing like that. I talk the exact same way I always have. And nobody has said anything about my personality changing or me acting different, either. I'm pretty much the exact same guy I was before we moved, just dealing with those little slip-ups I told you about.

Around the time you moved to the condo a year ago, did you experience any head injuries, falls, or head trauma? And have you noticed any unusual smells, or has anyone mentioned concerns about the condo itself — like water damage, mold, or anything like that?

No, no head injuries or falls... nothing like that. I haven't hit my head at all. And the condo is in really good shape. I haven't noticed any weird smells, and there's no water damage or mold or anything. We had it all checked out before we moved in, so... no, none of that.

When you're doing something that requires careful attention to detail — like reading instructions, paying bills, or following a recipe — do you find yourself making mistakes there too, or is it mainly just with those quick, everyday tasks you mentioned?

Yeah, it happens with that kind of stuff too. Honestly, that's a big part of what brings me in. I just keep messing up little things when I have to pay close attention. 

Like, I'll be looking at a schedule and write down the exact wrong time on a senior-center class sheet. Or I'll be working on a project, measure a board once, and still end up cutting it a hair short just because I skipped over the small print in the instructions. So, yeah, it definitely happens when I'm trying to focus on the details, too.

You mentioned the mistakes have stayed about the same level since the move. But thinking back over these past 12 months, would you say your ability to catch those small details has gotten noticeably worse compared to where you were 6 months ago, or has it truly remained unchanged?

No, I wouldn't say it's gotten worse. It's really just... stayed the same. Looking back, you know, six months ago versus now, it feels pretty much identical. I haven't noticed it getting harder to catch things recently or any big drop-off. It's just been that same steady level of messing up those little details for the whole year we've been here.

Thinking back further — say, 2 or 3 years before you moved to the condo — do you remember whether you were making these same kinds of careless mistakes with details back then, or was your attention to detail noticeably better at that time?

Well, honestly, it's always been this way. Even way back before we moved, two, three, maybe ten years ago... it's never really been any different. My wife will tell you, I've always been the guy who misses the details. 

Actually, it goes back a lot further than that. Even when I was just a kid, in elementary school, I remember my teachers would write on my report cards that I was a bright kid, but... I was always forgetting my books, losing my homework, that sort of thing. They'd say I'd just sit there staring out the window unless somebody was right there keeping me on track. So, yeah, it's definitely not a new thing for me.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a lifelong pattern of inattention, carelessness with details, and difficulty maintaining focus that began in childhood (elementary school reports document forgetfulness, losing homework, and needing external structure to stay on task). These symptoms have persisted consistently into adulthood across multiple decades and contexts (work projects, administrative tasks, attention-to-detail activities). While the patient attributes recent worsening to the move one year ago, detailed questioning reveals the symptoms have remained stable at the same level for the past 12 months and have always been present throughout his life. The chronic, pervasive nature of inattentive symptoms beginning in childhood and continuing into adulthood, combined with functional impairment (mistakes affecting work projects and daily tasks), is consistent with Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder, Predominantly Inattentive Presentation (F90.9). No evidence of recent neurological event, head trauma, mood disorder, or progressive cognitive decline was identified.
